questions.q:
With reference to the status of the India-EU FTA as of January 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It had entered into force after approval by the European Parliament.
2. Approval on the EU side requires unanimity of every member State in the Council and needs no consent from the Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. What was announced at the 16th Summit was the conclusion of negotiations. Legal scrubbing and translation come next, followed by approval by the Council through a qualified majority and consent of the European Parliament, and then ratification by India. One passage in a magazine calls the deal signed, so careful reading matters. Vision warns that full impact could take 5 to 10 years.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 20-23; Shankar IAS pp. 34-36; Vision IAS pp. 18-20

questions.q:
In the context of India-EU nuclear cooperation, consider the following statements:
1. Euratom was set up by the Treaty of Rome, 1957.
2. India and Euratom have a research and development agreement dating from July 2020.
3. India has been a full Member State of CERN since 2017.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 fails because India became an Associate Member of CERN in 2017, not a full Member State. Euratom promotes peaceful nuclear use, research and knowledge-sharing and aims to prevent diversion to military use. This cooperation runs alongside trade and defence tracks, showing how far the relationship has moved beyond the FTA alone.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 20-23; Shankar IAS pp. 34-36

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism remains a concern for Indian exporters despite the India-EU FTA.
Statement-II: The FTA's tariff elimination automatically exempts Indian goods from the carbon levy.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: CBAM falls on steel, aluminium, cement and similar goods, and brings compliance costs and heavy data reporting. Statement-II is wrong because a carbon levy is separate from customs duty, so zero tariffs under the deal do not remove it. India had sought safeguards on this. It is also why a headline figure of duty-free access can overstate the real gain for carbon-intensive exporters.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 20-23; Shankar IAS pp. 34-36

questions.q:
Germany has said it intends to join certain Indian-led forums. Consider the following pairs:
Forum : Character
1. Tarang Shakti : Exercise of the Indian Army
2. MILAN : Exercise of the Indian Navy
3. Indian Ocean Naval Symposium : Maritime forum of navies in the region
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2 and 3 are correct. Pair 1 is wrong because Tarang Shakti is an air-combat exercise of the Indian Air Force. Participation in these shows a European power's growing interest in the Indo-Pacific. It was accompanied by a Joint Declaration of Intent on a Defence Industrial Cooperation Roadmap covering co-development and co-production, plus a new bilateral Indo-Pacific consultation mechanism.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Venezuela produces less than one per cent of world oil despite its very large proven reserves.
Statement-II: US sanctions, economic crisis and chronic under-investment have held down its output.
Statement-III: Saudi Arabia holds larger proven reserves than Venezuela, which limits Venezuela's output.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and that one explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statements I and II are correct, and II explains I. Statement-III is wrong because Saudi Arabia, the largest exporter, stands second to Venezuela in proven reserves. In any case, reserves in another country would not explain low output. Most Venezuelan reserves lie in the Orinoco Belt. Output of about 1 million barrels a day compares with global output above 100 million, so any quick effect on world supply would be modest.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 23-25; Shankar IAS pp. 23-25

questions.q: The 'Chevron model', which ONGC would like to use in Venezuela, refers to
o: the transfer of PDVSA's reserves to a UN-supervised trust
a swap of Venezuelan crude for refined products at a fixed price
a joint venture in which the foreign firm must hold a majority over PDVSA
foreign firms operating oil assets after specific US approval, despite sanctions
questions.e: Chevron was the first to operate this way. A specific licence from OFAC gives a foreign firm wide control over finance, operations and marketing even though PDVSA remains majority shareholder, so a foreign majority is not the point. Without such a licence, firms cannot use US banking or dollars. Swap arrangements and a UN trust are not part of this model. For India, this route could help recover stuck dividends.

questions.q:
In the context of the Commonwealth Speakers' Conference, consider the following statements:
1. Its 29th edition is to be held in London in 2028.
2. Its Standing Committee is chaired by the Presiding Officer of the previous host.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The Standing Committee is chaired by the Presiding Officer of the next host, not the previous one, so it can shape the coming agenda. India chaired the meeting at Guernsey in January 2025 for that reason. The 28th Conference discussed artificial intelligence in legislatures, social media and parliamentary discourse, public understanding of Parliament, and the wellbeing of members and staff.

questions.q: India and Germany set up a 'Track 1.5' Foreign Policy and Security Dialogue. 'Track 1.5' diplomacy means
o: dialogue among private citizens with no officials present
formal negotiations between Heads of Government only
semi-formal dialogue with officials and non-governmental experts together
negotiations mediated by a third country under UN auspices
questions.e: Track 1 is formal diplomacy between governments, and Track 2 is unofficial dialogue among experts and citizens. Track 1.5 sits in between, with officials and non-governmental experts together in a semi-formal setting, allowing ideas to be tested without commitment. UN mediation is a different mechanism altogether. This dialogue sits alongside a Defence Roadmap and agreements on semiconductors and critical minerals.

questions.q:
In the context of India's ties with the Arab world, consider the following statements:
1. Duqm port, whose access aids the Indian Navy, lies in Oman.
2. IMEC was launched at the G20 New Delhi Summit in 2023.
3. India's strategic partnership with Egypt dates from 2008, ahead of those with Oman and the UAE.
4. UPI is accepted in Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 fails because the 2008 partnership is with Oman, followed by the UAE in 2015, while Egypt's dates from 2023. Duqm helps the Navy to operate and to keep watch on China's navy in the region. UPI acceptance extends the earlier spread of RuPay and rupee-dirham settlement. The region also supplies about 60 per cent of India's crude imports, which explains the weight given to these ties.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly arranges forms of economic integration from the shallowest to the deepest?
o: Preferential Trade Agreement, Free Trade Agreement, Customs Union, Common Market, Economic Union
Free Trade Agreement, Preferential Trade Agreement, Customs Union, Economic Union, Common Market
Preferential Trade Agreement, Free Trade Agreement, Common Market, Customs Union, Economic Union
Preferential Trade Agreement, Customs Union, Free Trade Agreement, Common Market, Economic Union
questions.e: A preferential agreement cuts tariffs on specific goods, and a free trade agreement cuts them on most goods. A customs union adds a common external tariff. A common market adds free movement of labour and capital. An economic union adds shared institutions. Each stage keeps what came before and surrenders more national control, so the EU, with its single market and institutions, stands at the deep end of this ladder.

questions.q:
With respect to China's drills around Taiwan, consider the following statements:
1. The trigger cited for 'Justice Mission-2025' was a proposed US arms sale of about 11 billion dollars to Taiwan.
2. 'Strait Thunder-2025A' was the drill that followed US Speaker Nancy Pelosi's visit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Beijing sees the sale, which covers howitzers, rocket systems and missile platforms, as violating the One-China principle. Statement 2 fails because the Pelosi visit was in 2022, whereas Strait Thunder was held in April 2025. On the first day of the December drills, 90 of the 130 air sorties crossed the Strait's centreline, a tacit boundary that China seeks to normalise crossing.

questions.q:
In the debate on what global indices measure, consider the following pairs:
Measure : Focus or criticism
1. Gross Domestic Product : Fully deducts ecological damage and the cost of inequality from output
2. Global Firepower : Ranks military strength, so it is said to reward arms races
3. V-Dem and Freedom House : Criticised by the Global South for neglecting non-Western contexts
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2 and 3 are correct. Pair 1 fails because GDP counts output and ignores ecological damage, inequality and the costs of growth, which is the standard critique. Hard-power rankings are said to reward arsenals rather than peace-building. The normative indices are criticised for bias, opaque methods and for privileging liberal individualism over collective welfare. These limits form the case made for the Responsible Nations Index.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 17-18; V-Dem and Freedom House focus is static

questions.q:
With reference to Greenland, consider the following statements:
1. It forms part of the GIUK Gap, a contested corridor for tracking submarines in the North Atlantic.
2. It hosts Pituffik Space Base, part of the US early-warning radar network.
3. Kvanefjeld and Kringlerne in its south are known for rare earth deposits.
4. It is an autonomous territory of Norway.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 fails because Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark, which is why the Danish PM was at the centre of the dispute. Pituffik is seen as vital for the proposed 'Golden Dome' system. Kvanefjeld also holds uranium. Together these points explain why location, minerals and missile defence are all part of the US interest.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 25-26; Greenland's status is static

questions.q:
Which of the following were among the bodies named in the US decision of January 2026 to end participation?
1. UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
2. Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
3. International Telecommunication Union
4. International Maritime Organization
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The climate treaty body and the IPCC were on the list, and the exit is said to leave a budget gap of about 22 per cent for them. The ITU and the IMO were not. The US still wants more influence in those two, because they set technical standards where it competes with China. A careless reader who assumes a blanket exit from all UN bodies would tick everything here.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 26-28; Shankar IAS pp. 25-26

questions.q:
With reference to the European Union, consider the following statements:
1. It traces its founding to 1951, when six countries including Italy and Luxembourg came together.
2. The UK left it on 31 January 2020.
3. The euro, launched in 1999, is used by all of its member States.
4. The Schengen arrangement dates from 1985.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 fails because the euro area covers 21 of the 27 members, so currency union and EU membership are not the same thing. Schengen is another separate layer, with Cyprus and Ireland outside it per the source, which shows the Union as overlapping circles of integration. The six founders were Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 20-23; Shankar IAS pp. 34-36

questions.q:
Spain has joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative. Consider the following statements:
1. The Initiative is a treaty-based arrangement launched at the Shangri-La Dialogue.
2. It builds on the idea of SAGAR, 'Security and Growth for All in the Region', of 2015.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The Initiative is a non-treaty, voluntary arrangement launched by India at the East Asia Summit in Bangkok in 2019, so statement 1 fails on both counts. It has seven pillars, including maritime security and maritime ecology. Its voluntary nature lets non-regional partners such as Spain join in chosen areas, and it fits with India's wish to keep the Indo-Pacific free, open and rules-based.

questions.q:
In the context of the League of Arab States, consider the following statements:
1. Decisions of its Council bind all members, whether or not they voted for them.
2. Votes in its Council are weighted according to a member's population.
3. Comoros and Mauritania are outside its membership.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Each member has one vote, so voting is not weighted, and decisions bind only the States that voted for them. That rule explains why the League often struggles to act as one bloc. Comoros and Mauritania are both members, among the 22 stretching across the Middle East and North Africa. Membership is broader than many assume, reaching East Africa through Somalia and Djibouti.

questions.q:
Critics called the US strikes on Venezuela a breach of the UN Charter. Consider the following pairs:
Provision : Subject
1. Article 2(4) : Refraining from the threat or use of force
2. Article 51 : Inherent right of individual or collective self-defence
3. Article 27 : Voting in the Security Council
4. Chapter VI : Enforcement action involving the use of armed force
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Pair 4 fails because Chapter VI deals with pacific settlement of disputes, and enforcement action belongs to Chapter VII. Article 27 is where the permanent members' veto comes from, which often stalls Council action. Self-defence and Security Council authorisation are the two accepted exceptions to the ban on force, which is why the legal debate has turned on them.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 23-25; Shankar IAS pp. 23-25; Charter provisions are static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India signed the Pax Silica Declaration to secure technology supply chains and reduce coercive dependencies.
Statement-II: The word 'Silica' in the name refers to a key compound used in chip-making.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but the origin of a name does not explain a policy decision. India's reasons lie elsewhere: China's use of rare earths as leverage, including its 2025 suspension of exports, and the pandemic lesson about depending on one country. 'Pax' is the Latin word for peace. The two statements are each true and related, yet the second gives no reason for the first, which is the distinction this format tests.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 30; Shankar IAS pp. 27-28

questions.q:
With reference to India's stake in Venezuela's oil sector, consider the following statements:
1. ONGC Videsh holds stakes in the San Cristobal and Carabobo-1 projects.
2. Reliance Industries was a regular buyer of Venezuelan crude before US sanctions in 2019.
3. The Office of Foreign Assets Control, whose licence is needed by firms under sanctions, is part of the US Treasury.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. ONGC Videsh, the overseas arm of ONGC, could recover over 500 million dollars in stuck dividends if sanctions ease. The near-term effect on India is minimal, because Indian refiners do not currently import Venezuelan crude. Over time, more supply could put downward pressure on oil prices, which would help India, as it imports over 88 per cent of its oil needs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Indian technology firms serving European clients face higher costs than those from countries that the EU treats as secure for data.
Statement-II: The EU has not granted India 'data secure' status under the GDPR.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Without that status, firms must add contractual and compliance steps before personal data can move to India. The FTA does not solve this by itself. Other services hurdles include limits on remote delivery and high minimum-salary thresholds for EU visas, which is why India seeks Mutual Recognition Agreements in medicine, engineering and accountancy.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 20-23; Shankar IAS pp. 34-36

questions.q:
With the 2nd India-Arab Foreign Ministers' Meeting in view, consider the following statements about the Arab League:
1. India is an observer in the League.
2. Syria was readmitted in May 2023 after a suspension of about 12 years.
3. Algeria and Morocco are among its founding members.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 fails because Algeria and Morocco joined only after gaining independence, and neither was among the founders of 1945. The founders named are Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Syria and Yemen. Brazil, Eritrea and Venezuela are other observers. India's observer status supports the institutional dialogue that began with a Memorandum of Understanding in March 2002.

questions.q:
With reference to the recommendations of the High-Level Advisory Group chaired by Surjit Bhalla, consider the following statements:
1. It advised India to keep services out of future agreements and limit them to goods.
2. It proposed a five-year FTA negotiation programme based on complementarity and sustainability.
3. It favoured trade-remedy provisions such as anti-dumping within FTAs, used on scientific economic evidence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is the opposite of its advice: the group wanted integrated coverage of goods, services and investment, with stakeholder consultation before finalising a deal. It also wanted a database on FTA use and an awareness drive for MSMEs. These matter because only 5 to 25 per cent of Indian exporters use the preferences on offer, owing to complex compliance and poor awareness.

questions.q:
With reference to the phases and effects of globalisation, consider the following statements:
1. The modern order assumed free movement of both capital and people across borders.
2. The mid-20th century order rested on the UN and the Bretton Woods institutions as a normative framework.
3. Returns to capital outpacing wages contributed to the rise of populism.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 fails because the assumption was free movement of capital but not of people, an asymmetry at the heart of the critique. Manufacturing shifted and migration became a political issue. China gained from open markets and technology while keeping State control of capital, labour and information. Its export-led model is said to have stunted industrialisation in poorer countries, including India.

questions.q:
Regarding the Board of Peace for Gaza, consider the following statements:
1. The 20-point Gaza plan also set in motion a National Committee for the Administration of Gaza and an International Stabilization Force.
2. India attended the Board's inaugural meeting in Washington D.C. as a full member.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. India took part as an observer, so statement 2 fails. The plan was endorsed by Security Council Resolution 2803 of 2025. Critics fear a leader-centric body could undermine international law, lack the checks of the General Assembly and marginalise the Global South through limited or possibly paid membership. Supporters point to speed and results compared with the UN's consensus model.

questions.q:
With reference to reported reactions to the US strikes on Venezuela, consider the following pairs:
Country : Reaction
1. Argentina : Supported the action as a step against narcotics and terror
2. India : Expressed deep concern and urged peaceful dialogue
3. Mexico : Supported the action alongside Israel and Paraguay
4. Chile : Criticised the action
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Pair 3 fails because Mexico was among the Latin American critics along with Colombia, Brazil, Chile, Panama and Cuba, and the supporters named were Argentina, Paraguay and Israel, so the region itself was divided. India reaffirmed sovereignty and non-intervention. The UN Secretary-General voiced alarm over use-of-force rules, while European States were cautious, avoiding strong condemnation.

questions.q: The return to 'mercantilism', discussed in the context of the end of globalisation, implies that a country
o: removes tariffs unilaterally to maximise consumer welfare
treats trade surpluses as strength and uses trade as an instrument of national power
hands trade policy to a supranational authority
leaves exchange rates and capital flows wholly to market forces
questions.e: Mercantilist thinking sees exports and surpluses as national strength and deficits as weakness, which matches the framing that trade is now about power and not cooperation. Unilateral tariff removal and hands-off capital flows describe free-market liberalism. Handing policy to a supranational authority is deep integration. The argument is that major economies now treat cooperation as a cost, and that low State capacity carries long-term risk for India.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 38-40; meaning is static

questions.q:
With reference to reported US conduct in January 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Its approach in Venezuela has been described as regime management, keeping the State and army while managing outcomes.
2. The US National Security Strategy 2025 formally renounced the Monroe Doctrine.
3. Critics also cited threats over Greenland and the suggestion that Canada become the '51st state' as erosion of sovereignty.
4. The Security Council authorised the Venezuela operation in advance.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is the opposite of the commentary, which treats the strategy as a revival of hemispheric hegemony. Statement 4 fails because critics complain that the Security Council was bypassed, and the Secretary-General voiced alarm that use-of-force rules were not respected. Together these points explain why the episode is read as weakening multilateralism and not merely as a bilateral dispute over oil.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 23-25; Shankar IAS pp. 23-25; Vision IAS pp. 25-26

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Loss of Greenland's ice would tend to amplify regional warming.
Statement-II: Ice reflects more solar radiation than the darker land or sea exposed when it melts.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I. This is the albedo effect: as bright ice disappears, darker surfaces absorb more heat, which melts more ice in a feedback loop. Greenland also matters because a full melt would raise sea level by more than 7 metres, and its ice cores are a climate archive reaching back hundreds of thousands of years.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 25-26; mechanism is static

questions.q: The 'Data Embassies' discussed during the UAE President's visit to India are best described as
o: tax-free zones for foreign data-centre operators
undersea cable landing stations jointly owned by two countries
consular offices that issue digital visas
offshore centres where a State stores critical data to ensure continuity and sovereignty
questions.e: A data embassy holds a State's critical records abroad so that government can continue after a cyberattack, disaster or conflict at home, while keeping sovereign control. Visa offices and cable landing stations have nothing to do with this function. Tax-free zones concern investment, not sovereignty. It forms part of a wider technology agenda with the UAE, which includes a supercomputing cluster under the IndiaAI Mission.

questions.q:
With respect to the WEF's Global Risks Report 2026 as it relates to India, consider the following statements:
1. Rising sea level is named as India's leading risk.
2. Insufficient public services and social protection appear among India's major risks.
3. The report recommends abandoning existing multilateral institutions in favour of new blocs.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. India's major risks are cyber insecurity, inequality in wealth and income, and insufficient public services and social protection, so sea level is not the leading item. Statement 3 reverses the advice, which is to reinforce existing multilateral institutions, prefer economic inducements with mutual gains and invest in local resilience. Domestic capacity therefore features as strongly as geopolitics in India's risk picture.

questions.q:
With reference to the Bhalla advisory group's advice on trade agreements, consider the following statements:
1. In GATS terms, it asked India to move beyond commercial presence towards the movement of natural persons.
2. It favoured a 'whole of government' approach involving ministries and States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 reverses the direction: the advice is to go beyond Mode 4, the movement of persons, to Mode 3, commercial presence. India has traditionally pressed for Mode 4 access, so the shift links services more closely with investment, in line with the group's call for integrated coverage. It also wanted stakeholder consultation before finalising a deal and a database on FTA utilisation.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 18-20; Modes 1 and 2 are static

questions.q:
With reference to India-Germany relations, consider the following statements:
1. Germany accounts for over half of India's trade with the European Union.
2. Indian passport holders were offered visa-free transit in Germany.
3. Germany is the largest source of FDI into India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Germany accounts for over a quarter of India's trade with the EU, with bilateral trade above 50 billion dollars in 2024, so statement 1 overstates it. It was the ninth-largest FDI source in 2024, so statement 3 fails too. Other links include the Green and Sustainable Development Partnership, the Indo-German Science and Technology Centre and a higher education roadmap.

questions.q:
Rockets in China's 'Justice Mission-2025' landed in Taiwan's contiguous zone. Consider the following pairs under UNCLOS, measured from the baselines:
1. Territorial sea : Up to 12 nautical miles
2. Contiguous zone : Up to 24 nautical miles
3. Exclusive Economic Zone : Up to 350 nautical miles
4. Continental shelf : Can extend up to 350 nautical miles in certain cases
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Pair 3 is wrong because the EEZ extends up to 200 nautical miles, and the figure of 350 belongs to an extended continental shelf, which is the usual confusion. In the contiguous zone a State can act to prevent breaches of customs, fiscal, immigration or sanitary laws. Rockets landing there were the closest ever, signalling precision-strike ability and maritime denial without entering territorial waters.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 28-30; UNCLOS limits are static

questions.q:
In the context of Pax Silica and related initiatives, consider the following statements:
1. Its inaugural summit was convened by the US in Washington D.C. on 12 December 2025.
2. Taiwan and the OECD are among its observers.
3. India was already part of the Supply Chain Resilience Initiative of 2021.
4. The 'India-US AI Opportunity Partnership' is a bilateral addendum to India's joining the initiative.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. Canada and the EU are the other observers. India was not invited to the inaugural summit but signed later. Earlier initiatives include the Supply Chain Resilience Initiative and the Quad Critical Minerals Initiative of 2025. India's interest grew after disruption in rare-earth magnet imports from China hit automobiles and electronics. Joining still raises questions about strategic autonomy, subsidies and procurement preferences.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 30; Shankar IAS pp. 27-28

questions.q:
With India now having trade agreements with most RCEP members, consider the following statements:
1. After the New Zealand deal, China is the only RCEP member with which India has no FTA.
2. Widening trade deficits are a concern under India's earlier agreements with ASEAN, Japan and South Korea.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. India stayed out of RCEP in 2019, mainly over cheap imports and a widening deficit, particularly with China. Since then it has reached much the same markets through separate agreements, without opening up to China on the same terms, and New Zealand completed the set. The deficit worry persists because older FTAs have not delivered balanced gains, and exporters' utilisation of preferences remains low.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 18-20; India's 2019 exit is static

questions.q:
With reference to the International Solar Alliance and the US exit, consider the following statements:
1. The Alliance builds and owns solar plants in its member countries.
2. The US joined it only in 2021.
3. China holds about 70 per cent of global solar cell capacity.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Alliance does not build plants. It facilitates low-cost finance, de-risks private investment and supports policy, training and capacity building. The US contribution was about 2.1 million dollars over three years, about 1 per cent of funding, so operations are little affected. The real risk lies in Africa and other poorer regions, if lenders turn cautious on cheap international finance.

questions.q:
In the context of Indo-Pacific frameworks, consider the following pairs:
Acronym : Associated with
1. AOIP : ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific
2. AIIPOIP : Australia-India partnership under the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative
3. IPEF : A US-led Indo-Pacific economic framework
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. Each framework overlaps with India's initiative in a different way. ASEAN's outlook stresses its own centrality, Australia and India have a dedicated partnership, and IPEF is economic and led by the US. India and Vietnam also agreed in 2020 to align cooperation with the Initiative. The Indo-Pacific matters because it holds more than half of the world's people and about two-thirds of the global economy.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 30-31; IPEF's US lead is static

questions.q: The EU-India Security and Defence Partnership, signed at the 16th India-EU Summit, is the EU's third such partnership in Asia, after those with
questions.e: The EU had earlier signed such partnerships with Japan and South Korea, and India is the third. The other names are plausible because Australia and Singapore are also close Indo-Pacific partners of the EU, but they do not fit here. The Indian partnership covers counter-terrorism, Indo-Pacific maritime security, cybersecurity and technology co-development, and it gives India's defence industry an opportunity in European markets.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 20-23; Shankar IAS pp. 34-36

questions.q:
In the context of the Greenland dispute, consider the following statements:
1. Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty concerns a member's right to withdraw from NATO.
2. The 1951 defence agreement relevant to Greenland was concluded between the United States and Canada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Article 5 is the collective defence clause, under which an attack on one member is treated as an attack on all, and Denmark signalled it would invoke it. The 1951 agreement is between the United States and Denmark, and renegotiating it to allow more US bases is one de-escalation idea. The Danish PM said a US attack would mean the end of NATO and of the post-War security order.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 25-26; Article 5 content is static

questions.q:
India objected to China's infrastructure projects in the Shaksgam Valley. Consider the following statements:
1. The area is also known as the Trans-Karakoram Tract.
2. It lies on both sides of the Shaksgam River.
3. It is bounded by the Kun Lun mountains and the Karakoram range.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The Valley lies north of the Karakoram watershed and adjoins the Siachen Glacier, which gives it a military importance beyond its size. India regards it as an integral part of its territory, occupied by Pakistan after 1947 and illegally ceded to China in the 1963 boundary agreement. Infrastructure there therefore raises both a sovereignty issue and a concern about China-Pakistan collusion.

questions.q:
With respect to India-UAE relations, consider the following statements:
1. Advanced nuclear technologies including Small Modular Reactors are to be explored following the SHANTI Act, 2025.
2. The UAE is consistently India's largest trading partner and largest export destination.
3. Bharat Mart, the Virtual Trade Corridor and Bharat-Africa Setu are meant to open new markets.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is wrong: the UAE is India's third-largest trading partner and second-largest export destination, not the largest on either count. Statement 1 is correct, since the two sides agreed to explore advanced nuclear technologies after the 2025 law. Statement 3 is correct, and these platforms support the wider trade target. The UAE also supplies crude, LNG and LPG and helps build India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 31-32; Shankar IAS p. 37

questions.q:
With reference to efforts to de-escalate over Greenland, consider the following statements:
1. 'Arctic Sentry' is a mission proposed by NATO allies to boost surveillance of ships and submarines in the High North.
2. Akrotiri and Dhekelia, cited as a model for US bases in Greenland, are UK sovereign base areas in Malta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Akrotiri and Dhekelia lie in Cyprus, so statement 2 fails on location. The model would give the US control of small sovereign areas, as one way of renegotiating the 1951 defence agreement. 'Operation Arctic Endurance' is a different item, the show of solidarity by European States. Keeping the names apart, along with the talks on a framework deal, is what this topic demands.

questions.q:
With reference to the 'Third Path' set out by Canada's Prime Minister, consider the following statements:
1. Its 'value-based realism' rules out working with partners who hold different values.
2. It was set out at the World Economic Forum in 2026.
3. Its 'variable geometry' means different coalitions for different issues, as with the Schengen Area, the G7 and the Quad.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is the reverse of the idea: value-based realism defends core principles such as sovereignty and human rights while accepting incremental progress, divergent interests and partners with different values. It also rests on building domestic strength. India is often named among the middle powers, alongside Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea, Indonesia and Brazil, which lack system-dominating power but carry real weight.

questions.q:
Arrange the following episodes of Chinese pressure on Taiwan in chronological order:
1. Drills after Tsai Ing-wen met Kevin McCarthy
2. 'Strait Thunder-2025A'
3. Missile firing after Nancy Pelosi's visit
4. 'Justice Mission-2025'
Select the correct order:
questions.e: The Pelosi visit came in 2022 and led to carrier groups, nuclear submarines and 11 missiles being fired into surrounding waters. The Tsai-McCarthy meeting drew drills in April 2023. 'Strait Thunder' came in April 2025, and 'Justice Mission' on 29-30 December 2025. The trend shows drills treated as a form of strategic punishment, growing into a continuum of coercive diplomacy, with each round normalising closer activity.

questions.q:
With reference to the WEF's Global Risks Report 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Over the long term, to 2036, its list is led by adverse outcomes of frontier technologies.
2. Geoeconomic confrontation refers to the use of economic tools to reshape cross-border ties, restricting flows of trade, technology, capital or knowledge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The long-term list is led by extreme weather events, followed by biodiversity loss and ecosystem collapse, so statement 1 fails. Geoeconomic confrontation tops the immediate list and aims to promote self-reliance, constrain rivals and consolidate spheres of influence. The report recommends inducements with mutual gains, reinforcing multilateral institutions and investing in local resilience.

questions.q:
Match List-I (doctrine) with List-II (central idea):
List-I
A. Gujral Doctrine
B. Monroe Doctrine
C. Carney Doctrine
D. 'Donroe' Doctrine
List-II
1. Non-reciprocal generosity to smaller neighbours and non-interference
2. No new European colonies in the Americas
3. Cooperation of middle powers in variable coalitions
4. Resource extraction and regime management through coercion
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: I.K. Gujral's approach to South Asia rested on non-interference, sovereignty and peaceful settlement, and it did not ask smaller neighbours for strict reciprocity. Monroe's 1823 message addressed European colonisation. Canada's PM set out the 'Third Path' at the World Economic Forum in 2026, built on value-based realism. 'Donroe' is the informal label for the present US approach in its near abroad.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 23-25; Shankar IAS pp. 23-25; Vision IAS p. 29; non-reciprocity is static

questions.q:
In the context of the legal framework for India's trade and investment treaties, consider the following statements:
1. Article XXIV of GATT allows FTAs as an exception to most-favoured-nation treatment if they cover substantially all trade.
2. The Enabling Clause lets developing countries cut tariffs on a limited set of products without opening the whole economy.
3. India's Model BIT 2015 lets a foreign investor begin investor-State arbitration without first using domestic remedies.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the rule: the Model BIT requires investors to exhaust domestic remedies first, and only then move to arbitration under frameworks such as UNCITRAL Rules or the ICSID Additional Facility Rules. Article XXIV also says barriers against non-members must not be raised. The Enabling Clause is the flexible route for developing countries, and it explains why partial agreements can still be WTO-compatible.

questions.q:
Match List-I (agreement) with List-II (feature highlighted):
List-I
A. India-Oman CEPA
B. India-New Zealand FTA
C. India-UK CETA
D. India-Australia ECTA
List-II
1. Social security exemptions
2. Visa quotas for Indian workers, with dairy kept out
3. Long-term stay for Indian professionals and 100 per cent FDI in key service sectors
4. Access to critical raw materials
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Oman's deal is known for professional stays and services FDI. New Zealand's completes India's coverage of RCEP members other than China, with worker visas and with dairy excluded. The UK agreement's distinctive labour gain is the social security exemption. Australia's agreement is framed around securing raw materials. Each deal reflects what the partner can offer, which is why mobility, resources and services figure differently from one to the next.

questions.q:
With reference to the Monroe and 'Donroe' doctrines, consider the following statements:
1. The Monroe Doctrine of 1823 included non-intervention by Europe in the Americas.
2. The 'Donroe Doctrine' is the formal title of the US National Security Strategy 2025.
3. The Monroe Doctrine included a promise of US non-interference in European wars and colonies.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 fails because 'Donroe' is an informal label after President Trump, not official policy, even though commentators tie it to the 2025 strategy. It describes transactional resource extraction, 'regime management' rather than regime change, and coercion through military threats and weaponised tariffs. The original Monroe Doctrine rested on non-colonisation, non-intervention by Europe and reciprocal US restraint.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 23-25; Shankar IAS pp. 23-25

questions.q:
With respect to Diego Garcia, consider the following statements:
1. It is a coral atoll in the central Indian Ocean, within the Chagos Archipelago.
2. It hosts a joint UK-US military facility.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Its central position makes it valuable for operations across West Asia and the Indian Ocean, which explains why the US President's criticism of the May 2025 UK-Mauritius agreement drew attention. The UK administered Chagos as the British Indian Ocean Territory from 1965. For India, the issue touches both support for Mauritius's sovereignty claim and the security balance in the region.

questions.q: Product-specific Rules of Origin in an agreement such as the India-EU FTA are primarily meant to
o: fix a uniform common external tariff for both partners
permit each partner to impose a carbon price on imports
ensure that services suppliers are recognised in each other's markets
prevent goods from third countries from gaining the agreement's preferences by routing through a partner
questions.e: Rules of origin decide when a product counts as made in a partner country, so third-country goods cannot claim lower duties by minor processing or transit. A common external tariff belongs to a customs union. Carbon pricing is the concern of the EU's CBAM. Recognition of professional qualifications is handled through Mutual Recognition Agreements. Complex rules can themselves become a burden, particularly for small exporters.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 20-23; Shankar IAS pp. 34-36; Vision IAS pp. 18-20

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In the Responsible Nations Index, the USA and China are ranked well below India.
Statement-II: The Index judges national strength by how responsibly a country treats its people, the planet and the international community, and not by economic or military size.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I. India is ranked 16th, the USA 66th and China 68th, because the framework moves the conversation from power to responsibility. So economic and military might does not automatically earn a high place. Supporters link this to the idea of India as a norm entrepreneur that separates a Great Power from a Good Power, and critics of older rankings see it as an alternative to Western-centric indices.

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes 'minilateralism', seen in bodies such as the Board of Peace?
o: A universal treaty open to all UN members
A bilateral agreement that is automatically extended to third parties
A voting rule under which the smallest States hold a veto
Cooperation among a small, selective group of States, often on a specific issue
questions.e: Minilateral bodies are small, selective and usually issue-based, which lets them move faster than universal institutions. The cost is legitimacy, since States left outside have no say. Universality is the feature they give up. Automatic extension to third parties describes most-favoured-nation treatment, and no such veto rule is part of the idea. The Quad and the G7 are often cited as similar arrangements and appear in the 'variable geometry' debate too.

questions.q:
With reference to the long-term national visions of Gulf States, consider the following pairs:
1. Saudi Arabia : Vision 2030
2. UAE : Centennial 2071
3. Kuwait : Vision 2035
4. Oman : Vision 2040
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four are correct. These visions aim to diversify Gulf economies away from oil, and they converge with India's goal of Viksit Bharat 2047. India is one of Saudi Arabia's eight strategic partners under its Vision 2030. This convergence underpins investment commitments such as those by the UAE and Saudi Arabia, mainly in infrastructure, as well as a shift of the relationship beyond energy buying.

questions.q: The Weimar Triangle, with which India's External Affairs Minister engaged for the first time, was set up in 1991 originally to
o: support reconciliation between Germany and Poland
coordinate eurozone fiscal policy among its largest members
manage Europe's defence-industrial exports to Asia
supervise the withdrawal of Soviet forces from Eastern Europe
questions.e: The grouping of France, Germany and Poland began in Weimar, Germany, to support German-Polish reconciliation after the Cold War, and now serves European integration, political dialogue and security cooperation. It is not a eurozone body, since Poland does not use the euro, and it is neither a defence-export arrangement nor a mechanism for Soviet withdrawal. India's engagement shows its growing interest in European groupings as well as individual States.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The US exit from the International Solar Alliance is not expected to change tariffs or project costs for Indian solar consumers.
Statement-II: India's solar industry depends mainly on the United States for its panels.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is wrong: India does not depend on the US for panels. Module capacity of about 144 GW and cell capacity of about 25 GW were reported by late 2025, and the import dependence that exists is on China. Investment is driven by domestic demand and long-term power purchase agreements, financed by Indian banks, global investors and development finance institutions.

questions.q:
Besides India, which of the following countries form the G4 that seeks reform of the UN Security Council?
1. Brazil
2. Germany
3. Japan
4. South Africa
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The G4 is India, Japan, Germany and Brazil, which support one another's claims to permanent seats. South Africa is not a member, though greater African representation is part of the same reform debate, and it is the natural trap. This came up after the Venezuela strikes because critics argued that the Security Council had been bypassed, and diluting the dominance of the five permanent members was offered as a remedy.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Even while ending participation in many bodies, the US still seeks more influence in standard-setting bodies such as the ITU and the ILO.
Statement-II: The US has declared all UN specialised agencies to be redundant and is leaving them together.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct and is described as selective multilateralism. Statement-II is wrong because the 66 bodies are a selected list of 35 non-UN organisations and 31 UN entities, and further reviews continue. The State Department labelled the listed bodies redundant, wasteful and contrary to US interests, but the label does not extend to all agencies. The approach is transactional, in line with 'America First'.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 26-28; Shankar IAS pp. 25-26

questions.q:
Most of India's trade with the Arab region passes through the Suez route. A ship going from India's west coast to the Suez Canal would pass through which of the following?
1. Arabian Sea
2. Gulf of Aden
3. Red Sea
4. Persian Gulf
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The route runs across the Arabian Sea, through the Gulf of Aden and the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, up the Red Sea and into the canal. The Persian Gulf lies off this route, reached through the Strait of Hormuz, and it matters for Gulf energy supplies instead. India's maritime security and anti-piracy efforts, as well as access to Duqm port in Oman, are closely tied to this geography.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 36-38; geography is static

questions.q:
With respect to the institutions of the European Union, consider the following pairs:
EU institution : Role
1. Court of Auditors : Interprets EU law and settles disputes between member States
2. European Commission : Proposes legislation and implements policies and the budget
3. European Parliament : Elected every five years
4. Court of Justice : Interprets EU law
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Pair 1 fails because interpreting EU law belongs to the Court of Justice, while the Court of Auditors checks the Union's finances. Both have 'Court' in the name, which invites the mistake. The European Council is the other main institution listed. These bodies matter to India because the FTA still has to pass through the EU's approval process before entry into force.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 20-23; Shankar IAS pp. 34-36; roles of the two courts are static

questions.q:
With reference to Taiwan, consider the following statements:
1. In the period reported, the DPP held the Executive Yuan while the Kuomintang and the Taiwan People's Party dominated the Legislative Yuan.
2. 'T-Dome' is a proposed multi-layered air-defence shield.
3. The Taiwan Relations Act is a law of the United States under which it provides material support.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The divided government is why progress on T-Dome has been slow. The Taiwan Relations Act is domestic US law and not a treaty with China or Taiwan, which allows arms support without formal recognition. The US played down the drills while continuing support. The Mainland Affairs Council, which handles cross-Strait policy, condemned the exercises as provocative and coercive.

questions.q:
With reference to India's engagement with the Arab League, consider the following statements:
1. India's Ambassador to Saudi Arabia was made its Permanent Representative to the League in December 2010.
2. The Arab-India Cooperation Forum, created in 2008, held its first meeting in Manama in January 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The Permanent Representative is India's Ambassador to Egypt, which follows from the League's headquarters being in Cairo, so statement 1 fails. The Forum took over seven years to hold its first meeting. A biennial Partnership and Investment Summit also runs alongside, and India-Arab Chambers of Commerce were to be inaugurated in 2026. Regional trade is over 240 billion dollars.

questions.q:
With reference to the India-EU FTA whose conclusion was announced at the 16th Summit, consider the following statements:
1. Social Security Agreements with all EU member States are envisaged within five years.
2. It has a dedicated chapter on Trade and Sustainable Development.
3. Intellectual property protection is to be under TRIPS.
4. India secured the opening of the EU's dairy market, while cereals remain protected on the EU side.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 fails because dairy is a sensitive sector that India itself kept out, along with cereals and some poultry, to protect its farmers. Mobility commitments also include post-study work visas and a framework for skilled professionals. The sustainability chapter covers environment, labour rights and climate cooperation. Autos and wine and spirits see phased cuts with quotas or safeguards, not immediate opening.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 20-23; Shankar IAS pp. 34-36

questions.q:
With reference to forms of trade integration, consider the following statements:
1. A customs union requires its members to apply a common external tariff.
2. A free trade agreement requires its members to give up separate tariffs on imports from non-members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. FTA partners cut duties among themselves but each keeps its own tariff against outsiders. That independence is why FTAs need rules of origin: without them, goods could enter through the lowest-tariff partner and move on duty-free. A customs union avoids this problem through a common external tariff, but it costs members their independent trade policy. India's recent deals are all of the FTA type.

questions.q:
In the context of US retreat from multilateral commitments, consider the following statements:
1. The US left the Paris Agreement for the second time in January 2026.
2. USAID, now dismantled, was the source of about two-fifths of UN-tracked humanitarian aid in 2024.
3. A study in The Lancet warned that Western aid cuts could cause over 22 million preventable deaths by 2030.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The climate exit is linked to opposition to what the US calls climate orthodoxy that hurts its fossil-fuel interests. USAID had 44.2 billion dollars in its 2024 budget. The effects are felt in health and humanitarian work, and the UN's regular budget is falling by 7 per cent in 2026, leading to cuts in staff and programmes. This creates room for other actors, including China, and adds to pressure for UN reform.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 26-28; Shankar IAS pp. 25-26

questions.q:
With reference to reports cited in recent international debates, consider the following pairs:
Report : Publisher
1. Global Risks Report 2026 : World Economic Forum
2. World Trade Report 2023 : UNCTAD
3. Responsible Nations Index : World Intellectual Foundation
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Pair 2 fails because the World Trade Report is a publication of the World Trade Organization, and its 2023 edition set out the idea of 're-globalisation' for resilient supply chains. UNCTAD's own products include the Global Investment Trends Monitor, which makes it a tempting wrong answer. Matching a report to its publisher is a common test, so keep a list as you go.

questions.q:
With reference to the Conference of Speakers and Presiding Officers of the Commonwealth, consider the following statements:
1. It has no formal affiliation with the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association or the Commonwealth Secretariat.
2. It meets every two years, with its Standing Committee meeting in the intervening year.
3. Its resolutions are not binding.
4. Deputy Speakers may substitute with full rights and are eligible for its Standing Committee.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 fails because Deputy Speakers can substitute with full rights but cannot serve on the Standing Committee. Membership overlaps with the other Commonwealth bodies, yet the forum stays independent, non-political and Speaker-led, which is the point of statement 1. Its resolutions carry normative weight only. The Standing Committee has 15 members and a quorum of 5.
